title: HDT update.yaml
description: One imported Windows update. Everything from baselineVersion downwards was read out of the package's own CompDB metadata rather than parsed from its file name; release is the administrator's, because no .msu says which product it is for.

id.description: The folder name under WindowsUpdates\ and the key a sequence selects.

kb.description: Read from the CompDB Feature/@FeatureID, never from the file name.

release.description: The os-releases.yaml id this update is filed under. THE ADMINISTRATOR'S, not the package's: nothing in a .msu distinguishes Windows 11 24H2 from Windows Server 2025.

kind.description: Read from Feature/@Type. This is what makes servicing-stack ordering exact rather than a guess at a file name.

fileName.description: The .msu as imported, beside this document. DISM is handed this file directly; the .wim inside it is rejected by /Add-Package with 0x80070057.

baselineVersion.description: CompDB @OSVersion - the build the update expects to find.

targetVersion.description: CompDB @TargetOSVersion - the build the update produces.

packageId.description: The package identity the update installs, used to verify the apply landed rather than trusting an exit code.

sourceBranch.description: The servicing branch token out of @TargetBuildInfo. Recorded and warned on, never matched.

enabled.description: Whether the ApplyUpdates step considers this update at all. An update is disabled rather than deleted when it is being taken out of service.

note.description: What the import wanted the administrator to know - a branch that disagreed with the release, or a release whose build was never measured.
